idiom_name: plain class over a Hash with a calls Array
implementation_notes: In Ruby the recording fake is an ordinary object: a Hash for state, an Array for the journal, and reader methods as the test-facing accessor - no interface declaration or framework is involved, so the classic structure collapses into a normal class. RSpec's message expectations and spies cover the recording half only when the collaborator may be replaced (expect(obj).to receive(:msg), allow plus have_received); use allow and spies rather than receive when the fake's behaviour must actually run, because receive replaces the implementation. Record plain value objects (Struct/Data or hashes) so equality reads well, build the fake per example, and use instance_double(RealClass) to keep the fake's interface honest against the real class.
pitfalls: A class variable (@@journal) or a constant-backed Hash is shared across examples - keep both store and journal in instance variables.
Pushing the same mutable Hash into the journal and mutating it later rewrites recorded history; record copies or frozen value objects.
RSpec's expect(...).to receive replaces the method, so the fake's behaviour is lost; use spies (allow plus have_received) when behaviour must run.
